datasource_item.source_question_text:
A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0. [incorrect]
B. 𝑣0 cos𝜃. [correct]
C. 𝑣0 sin𝜃. [incorrect]
D. 0. [incorrect]
datasource_item.generated_question_text:
A dolphin leaves the water with speed u0 at an angle ϕ above the horizontal. What is the dolphin’s speed at the highest point of its trajectory (ignore air resistance)?
A. u0 [incorrect] Explanation: This ignores that the vertical component of velocity decreases to zero at the peak.
B. u0 cos ϕ [correct] Explanation: At maximum height the vertical component is zero, so the remaining speed is the horizontal component u0 cos ϕ.
C. u0 sin ϕ [incorrect] Explanation: This gives the initial vertical component, which is not the speed at the peak.
D. 0 [incorrect] Explanation: Only the vertical velocity is zero at the top; the horizontal velocity is generally nonzero.
